title: ‘Elsinore’ Review: Andrew Scott’s Towering Performance as a Dying Actor Can’t Overcome AIDS-Movie Awards Bait Clichés
summary: Telluride: Scott vividly portrays "Gandhi" and "Chariots of Fire" star Ian Charleson, who made "Hamlet" his final role at the National Theatre, but the movie around him sinks into forgettability.

title: ‘The Idiot(s)’ Review: Johnny Flynn and Aimee Lou Wood Suffer Rapturously in Surreal Russian Lit Biopic
summary: Małgorzata Szumowska and Michał Englert’s Dostoevsky drama finds dark comedy in a brilliantly strange marriage, but strains to make that suffering meaningful.

title: This September, ‘Remember Me’: The 2010 Robert Pattinson Film That Sounds Like Something He Made Up
summary: Never forget Emilie de Ravin co-starring in this miserable love story from director Allen Coulter, technically about a guy who hates his dad and dates a cop's daughter for revenge.

title: ‘A Long Winter’ Review: Andrew Haigh Goes Cold with an Immaculately Crafted Coming-of-Age Story Too Restrained for Its Own Good
summary: Fred Hechinger and Eben Moss-Bachrach are terrific in a queer period drama about a young man trying to escape his father's shadow in 1950s Colorado.

title: ‘Tender Loving Care’ Review: Kate O’Flynn Astonishes in Mike Leigh’s Simple but Profoundly Moving Final Film
summary: A drama about a week in the life of two social workers, Leigh's supposed swan song pierces with the directness of a closing statement.

title: Inside the Telluride Opening Day Brunch: John Malkovich, Carrie Coon, and the Questions on Everyone’s Minds
summary: We take you inside the opening-day brunch in the Colorado mountains with the stars and filmmakers behind this year's lineup.

title: ‘Chronovisor’ Directors Measured Twice and Cut Film Once to Tell a Text-Based Thriller
summary: Directors Jack Auen and Kevin Walker tell IndieWire about using every page and graphic to spin a conspiracy thriller from the archival evidence of a time-travel hoax.

title: ‘The Basics of Philosophy’ Review: Paul Schrader’s Lurid Study of a Predatory Intellectual Is Quietly Explosive, but Not Dangerous Enough
summary: Venice: Jack Huston plays a philosophy professor reliving his past sins in a Schrader provocation that finds the director confronting his own.

title: ‘Furies’ Review: An Anarchic Lebanese Heist Thriller Blazes Past Borders and Genre Cliches
summary: Venice: George Clooney executive-produces this exuberantly directed and absorbing thriller about economic collapse in Beirut from director Rami Kodeih.

title: Abel Ferrara Only Went Hollywood Once, but It Resulted in a Horror Classic
summary: The maverick director of indie landmarks like "King of New York" and "The Bad Lieutenant" had a bad time in the studio system, but the movie that resulted — the 1993 horror film "Body Snatchers" — is a miracle of both personal expression and studio scale.

title: ‘Mr. Nelson, Did You Kill People?’ Review: Shinya Tsukamoto Directs a Bizarre Misfire About a Black Soldier in Vietnam
summary: Venice: Stilted dialogue, oppressive sound design, and a gawking cultural gaze yield one of the most unpleasant films of this year’s competition.

title: Director Michael Dinner Loves a Challenge — and He Had Plenty of Them on ‘Silo’
summary: Dinner tells IndieWire about his work on the ambitious Apple TV series, which forced him to wrap his head around a complex backstory and thousands of visual effects shots.
